title: the-corpus-is-out-of-proven-space
intention: settle what proven-space IS — a state the corpus rests in, or a fresh state a component enters when it is about to be leaned on — and enforce that answer with something other than a human remembering, so the measured fraction is what the rule predicts rather than an accident of who edited what last.
why: The lived symptom arrives the first time somebody outside this voyage tries to cross into a rest: clearance demands a proof standing in proven-space, they name their component's proof, and the door tells them the seal is green but the code has moved underneath it. Their ordinary crossing has become a re-seal errand, and nothing warned them, because the corpus reads green everywhere — 78 proofs with green seals beside them, 6 of which mean what a reader assumes all 78 mean.
traces_to: Law 3 (nothing is known until measured — 6 of 78 is the whole content of this, and nobody had counted)
Law 8 (nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass — this asks what STAYING there means)
Law 9 (red is the default; green is earned — a green seal over moved code is green that stopped being earned and nothing derived red)

falsifier.proves_green: code-seam@v2 gate-set, transcribed. PROVEME (non-skippable): proofs beside the code at cairn/devices/tester/proofs/, run twice, sealed under the tester with isolation='netns' and persisted through validation_store.persist_validation. The Law 8 teeth: (i) the census that produces the number is a tooth, not a script — it asserts INVARIANTS (every non-standing proof carries a why naming which of the four ways it failed; the standing set is a subset of the sealed set) rather than the snapshot value 6, because the number legitimately moves; (ii) whatever the settled rule is, a tooth that fails if the rule is reverted; (iii) a tooth over the four broken TRAILS asserting they are diagnosed rather than overwritten — the trail file before and after is byte-identical for its existing lines. BUILD GATE: the PROVEME crossing runs build_inspector over cairn/devices/tester at its own address. FEEDBACK TO ORIGIN ON FAILURE (Law 3+8 invariant): a red routes back to this ticket and to cairn/devices/tester/intention+why.json, whose horizon is what this node is measuring against.
falsifier.proves_red: DONE when the corpus has a STATED rule for what proven-space is (a resting state the corpus is held in, or a fresh state a component enters when it is about to be leaned on), that rule is enforced by something other than a human remembering, and the measured number is what the rule predicts rather than an accident. RED on any of: (1) the answer is a periodic re-seal sweep — a poll, which the standing shrinking-footprint aim refuses, and which manufactures the number it reports; (2) the number is raised by weakening standing() (dropping the fingerprint check, widening the horizon) — proven-space bought by lowering what proven means is the check going green for the wrong reason; (3) the four broken TRAILS are re-sealed rather than diagnosed, which would overwrite the evidence of a Law 7 integrity failure with a fresh green; (4) the rule lands and the number does not move, meaning the rule was written to describe what already happens. HORIZON: the first crossing that is REFUSED for an unproven proven_by after this ticket proves out. Until one exists, the rule is unexercised and its cost is unmeasured — and its cost is the whole question, because a seal decayed at the moment somebody needs it turns an ordinary crossing into a re-seal errand.

children: (a) what-proven-space-is-for — [ANSWERED 2026-09-02] proven-space is a per-component fresh state that decays, gated at crossing-time by clearance.py (lines 876-907). No population threshold follows because the gate is per-component, not population-wide — the fraction (88/175 measured 2026-09-02) is a diagnostic measure, not a gate. The sole consumer (clearance.py line 902) reads standing(proof_path) and raises Unproven if the seal is not green or the source fingerprint has moved. A re-seal sweep is not a fix — it manufactures a number that decays in minutes.

(b) four-seal-trails-do-not-verify — [RESOLVED 2026-09-02] resolved by ticket a-validation-is-one-current-record-not-a-trail (trail collapse). Census measurement: survey_the_corpus() returns trail_integrity_failures=[], 0 integrity failures across 175 proofs. All 7 inference_domain validations now hold exactly 1 record each, all green, all with source_fingerprint.

questions.a: Two assumptions were load-bearing and are now named. (1) THAT A GREEN SEAL MEANS PROVEN — it does not, and that is the design working: validation_store.standing() re-reads the source fingerprint the tester recorded, so a seal green on code that has since moved refuses. Measured 2026-08-10 across the corpus: 6 of 78 proofs stand in proven-space, and 4 of the 6 were sealed in the last hour by the voyage doing the measuring. Nearly the whole corpus is green-by-seal and red-by-fingerprint at once. (2) THAT THE FIX IS A RE-SEAL SWEEP — this is the assumption to kill loudly. Re-sealing 72 proofs in one act would put the whole corpus in proven-space for exactly as long as nobody edits anything, which is minutes; the number would be a snapshot of when the sweep ran, not a property of the corpus. What is actually unknown is whether proven-space is meant to be a state the corpus RESTS in or a state a component enters at the moment it needs to be leaned on. This ticket exists to settle that question first, and the sweep is downstream of the answer, not a substitute for it.

Two points I would have asserted wrapped and have not. (a) THE FOUR BROKEN SEAL TRAILS ARE A DIFFERENT DEFECT and are not counted in the 72. cairn/devices/inference_domain/validations/ carries four proofs whose failure is 'the seal trail ... ' — a TRAIL INTEGRITY refusal, not a stale fingerprint, which means the append-only chain itself does not verify. That is a Law 7 record-of-truth problem and it is louder than staleness; it is child (b) and it is the one to look at first. (b) WHAT PROVEN-SPACE IS FOR is genuinely open. Today exactly one consumer reads it — clearance.py's second refusal — so 'the corpus is out of proven-space' has one observable consequence: a crossing cannot be cleared onto a component whose seal has decayed. Whether that is a problem or the mechanism working correctly depends on the answer to the assumption above, and asserting it wrapped would be designing for a problem nobody has.

No exclusive-and-terminal collision; the congruency lab was recompiled and consulted 2026-08-10 before this cast, and no intention claims authority over what proven-space is for — cairn/devices/tester's charter owns the seal and the horizon, and this node is a question about the STATE those produce, so it berths under the tester rather than beside it. Two distinctions to record. (1) tickets/emit-refuses-an-uncleared-crossing (in flight, at WATCHME) is where this was measured, and it is the ticket that gave proven-space its first real consumer. Their whys are opposed only in appearance: that ticket needed the demanded set narrow enough that the corpus's staleness did not refuse the fleet, and it got there by scoping rather than by re-sealing — deliberately leaving this debt whole and filed rather than absorbing it. (2) cairn/devices/tester's own horizon already contemplates seal decay; this is not a second opinion about that, it is the corpus-wide COUNT the horizon never had, and the count is what makes the question answerable.

how: Settle what proven-space IS (a resting state or a fresh entry state). Enforce the answer: four seal trails that do not verify, and the leaning-on that depends on the answer. Children decompose the definition and the four trails.
priority: P2 — P2 because the state has exactly one consumer today (clearance.py's proven-space refusal) and the voyage that gave it that consumer routed around the debt honestly — by scoping the demanded set to the crossing into a rest, which /sail seals one step earlier, rather than by widening a roster. So nothing is currently blocked. It is not P3 because the number is 6 of 78 and the mechanism is now load-bearing on every crossing into proven-space: the first component that needs to cross and finds its seal decayed pays a re-seal errand, and falsifier clause (4) of the parent ticket names exactly that as a real red. CHILD (b) IS NOT P2 — four seal trails failing INTEGRITY is a Law 7 problem and should be looked at on its own clock.
workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> [WATCHME(proven-space-stays-populated):waiting] -> PROVED

watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact written against THIS ticket's falsifier, carrying the full census (every proof, standing or not, with the reader's why verbatim), the trail-integrity failures listed separately, and the refusal record if one exists.
watchme.consumer: the tester (cairn/devices/tester/), owner of the seal, the fingerprint and the horizon — the only component that can act on a finding about what its own seals mean. Law 6: the back-edge that re-opens this node is the owner's act, never the probe's.
watchme.enough: when at least one crossing has been refused for an unproven proven_by AND the standing fraction has held at or above the settled rule's prediction across that refusal — both halves required, because a corpus nobody leans on can sit at any fraction without the number meaning anything, and a fraction that holds only because nothing is being edited is a measurement of quiet, not of health.
watchme.nexus: hypothesize — 'is proven-space a state the corpus rests in, and did the settled rule actually keep it populated?' is a claim about an outcome, and the hypothesize tree is where this system's kills and confirmations already accumulate.
watchme.trigger: fires on any pulse reaching the tester's address, running validation_store.standing() over every proof under cairn/*/proofs/ — files only, no device, no network. It reports a finding on any of three conditions: (a) a proof's seal TRAIL fails integrity, which is a Law 7 record-of-truth failure and is reported alone, never folded into the staleness count; (b) the standing fraction falls below what the settled rule predicts, with the rule's own threshold read from where the rule is written rather than from a constant in the probe; (c) a crossing was REFUSED for an unproven proven_by — the horizon condition, and the only evidence that the state has an actual cost. Each finding carries the failing proofs verbatim with their component and the reader's own why string, so the consumer never re-derives them.

It is filed as an edge and not only as a falsifier clause because the same reflex will arrive at every state-that-decays in this system, and naming it once is cheaper than re-deriving it at each.
